restoring-equilibrium: Look for the square root in the spring-frequency rule before scaling the stiffness.
Mass is fixed. Which other factor sets the spring’s returning acceleration?
amplitude-phase: With the cycle time fixed, must the object cover more or less ground between the endpoints?
Compare two swings taking the same time but reaching different distances.
oscillator-initial-data: A minus sign on velocity switches direction. Does it change the size of the largest swing?
Check the squared starting position and squared starting velocity before adding.
small-pendulum: Does a shorter pendulum swing faster or slower? Recheck the length factor in the period.
Length occurs inside a square root. What happens to that root?
viscous-oscillator: Is the drag coefficient b above or below the fraction line in β = b/(2m)?
Keeping mass fixed does not freeze the drag. Which number changed?
damping-regimes: Compare b with twice the square root of mass × stiffness. On which side of that boundary is it?
Critical damping needs equality, not just a large drag value. Compare the two numbers.
damping-energy: Energy follows the square of the envelope. Apply the change to both amplitude factors.
If the swings die down, is there any source adding energy?
driven-amplitude: Locate the force amplitude in the numerator of the response rule.
The drive frequency stayed the same. Did the strength of the push stay the same?
driven-phase: At resonance, compare the timing of velocity with that of displacement. Do they peak together?
The spring moves while the driver supplies energy. At which instants does velocity vanish?
driven-power: The stronger drive changes both force and the resulting velocity amplitude. How does their product change?
Has the response speed stayed fixed in this linear model?
resonance-width: Find the width factor containing β in the weak-damping rule.
A smaller β means the system retains oscillations longer. Recheck which width describes the resonance.
two-mass-equations: Draw both carts before and after moving them. Did the distance between them change?
The spring senses the relative positions of its ends. How far did each end move?
symmetric-motions: In which shared motion do the carts stretch the middle spring?
Try opposite cart displacements. Does the middle spring then supply a restoring force?
mode-superposition: Add your predicted mode contributions to recover the measured starting positions. Do you get twice the displacement?
If only the together-moving pattern were present, where would the second cart start?
mode-eigenproblem: Hold the restoring force fixed. What does more mass do to acceleration?
Does the natural frequency depend on stiffness alone or on stiffness divided by mass?
modal-initial-data: Compare the signs of the two initial coordinates with the signs in the two mode patterns.
Can a nonzero starting displacement be represented with zero of every mode?
mode-driving: Dot the force vector with the mode whose carts move together. What happens to opposite terms?
Try the mode whose carts have opposite signs. Do its two force contributions cancel or reinforce?
travelling-profile: For a shape moving right, compare a fixed point with the shape just to its left a moment earlier.
The wave’s horizontal travel speed and the string’s vertical velocity are different quantities. Which uses slope?
string-wave-equation: Is mass per length above or below the fraction line in the wave-speed rule?
Does the square root apply before or after the mass ratio is used?
wave-phase-power: Count the factors of amplitude in the mean-power formula.
At the same frequency, do larger excursions leave the string’s moving parts with the same speeds?
string-interface: Label the new incident side before subtracting the two string properties.
Check numerator and denominator after reversing sides. Can the stated reflection ratio have that size?
standing-superposition: A repeating wave has how many neighboring node intervals per full wavelength?
A node-to-peak interval is different from a node-to-node interval. Which was requested?
boundary-spectra: Sketch the longest standing wave in a longer pipe. What happens to its wavelength?
Find frequency from speed divided by the wavelength that fits the new length.
string-mode-expansion: Match the factor 2πx/L to the mode patterns before assigning the coefficient.
Does the starting profile contain two different sine patterns, or one?
coherent-addition: Draw two equal wave arrows separated by half a turn before combining them.
Each amplitude is a length. Can adding two such arrows produce more than the sum of their lengths?
path-phase: Combine the supplied source phase with the phase gained through the path difference, using the convention in the example.
The path already adds a phase difference. Did you also include the source’s own phase?
beat-envelope: Count how often the two waves catch up with one another, rather than the half-rate of an envelope’s signed cosine.
A mean pitch and the rate of loudness changes answer different questions.
fourier-coefficients: Which multiple of a₀ appears as the constant part of this particular Fourier series?
Try substituting your a₀ back into the series. Does it give the stated constant voltage?
localized-packet: At zero wave number, how does the area under the box change?
Its height stays fixed. What else enters the integral of a box?
bandwidth-duration: The time width and frequency width have a fixed product for this pulse. Which way must the other width move?
Use the new time width in the formula rather than the old one.
longitudinal-sound: At fixed stiffness, compare the acceleration of denser fluid under the same restoring pressure.
Is density in the numerator or denominator beneath the square root?
sound-intensity: Intensity contains pressure squared. How many pressure factors are changing?
The medium sets one factor. Did the sound wave sending energy through it stay equally strong?
sound-boundaries: List the allowed harmonics for a pipe closed at one end before picking the second one.
Does the second allowed mode of this pipe fit four quarter-waves?
sound-doppler: With the source at rest, which part of the Doppler rule changes for the moving listener?
Does moving away make wave crests reach the listener more or less frequently?
dispersion-relation: The dispersion relation contains k squared. How many k factors triple?
Distinguish the numerical change in k from its ratio before scaling the square.
phase-group-speed: Are you using the slope dω/dk needed for group speed, or ω/k for a crest?
Differentiate the dispersion rule once and use the new centre wave number once.
packet-spreading: Does reversing the sign of D remove the spread already accumulated in the width formula?
See how D enters the square inside the width expression. Can its sign cancel the initial width?
cutoff-evanescence: You have a ratio of wave amplitudes. What extra operation is requested?
Squaring a ratio and multiplying it by two are different operations. Which is used for this question?
transverse-em-wave: Check the number of electric-field factors in the energy carried by the wave.
The wave speed stays fixed, but what happened to the energy in a given volume?
polarization-states: A circle needs two nonzero directions of oscillation. Which directions actually have amplitude?
Plot a point with y always zero while x varies. How many independent extents does it trace?
polarizer-projection: The incident light includes many field directions. Does a single filter transmit all their components?
For a given axis, do all the incoming vibration directions lie across it?
wavefront-refraction: Draw a crest arriving head-on at the interface. Which side of the crest enters first?
Look at Snell’s rule for a zero incoming angle before testing any critical-angle claim.
two-slit-interference: Is slit separation a multiplier or a divisor in the fringe-spacing rule?
Compare paths from the two slit centres when their spacing changes.
single-slit-diffraction: For the first dark direction, use width × absolute sine = wavelength. Which factor must compensate?
If the slit gets wider, does the light from its two ends still travel the same path difference at the old angle?
grating-resolution: Compare the smallest distinguishable wavelength gap with resolving power. Are they proportional or reciprocal?
The slit count enters the resolving-power formula even when the order does not change.
wave-model-selection: Does bulk sound use string tension and mass per length, or pressure response and volume density?
What material is disturbed in this setup? Does a vacuum contain that string?
wave-capstone: Tension enters the wave speed under a square root. Which quantities then set the string frequency?
The wavelength fitting the string is fixed. What happened to its wave speed?
wave-assessment: Which part of this setup determines the path differences between parts of the slit?
Light also changes brightness after the filter turns. Does changing brightness change the dark angle set by slit width and wavelength?
